newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary settles farm subsidy dispute with WTO.
newsitem.headline: Hungary settles farm subsidy dispute with WTO.

text.p: Hungary said on Thursday it had settled a two-year dispute with the World Trade Organisation (WTO) over the country's agricultural export subsidies.
"It was a success in the sense that we (Hungary) are no longer outside the regulations," Peter Balas, Deputy State Secretary at the Ministry for Industry, Trade and Tourism, told a news conference.
The dispute dates back to the Uruguay round of GATT talks, where Hungary submitted inaccurate export subsidy figures on which the later reduction of those subsidies was to be based, he said.

In 1992, Hungary only gave export subsidy figures for one product in each of the 16 product categories instead of all products. The figure given amounted to 22 billion forints instead of the actual 58 billion forints average of the years 1986 to 1990.
It then asked the WTO to set the 1995 subsidies of 45 billion forints as a base, with the figure to be calculated in dollar terms instead of the inflation-prone forint.
Hungarian inflation is currently running at 18.7 percent.
The WTO accepted Hungary's claim for a new base from which subsidies should be cut by 36 percent and the volume of subsidised exports by 21 percent by the year 2000.
The WTO also gave Hungary a two-year waiver until 2002, by which time the country should fully comply with regulations.
However, the WTO did not accept Hungary's request for the base export subsidy amount to be established in dollar terms.

Balazs Tarjan, head of the Agricultural Ministry's agricultural regime office said the outcome meant that Hungary would have to restructure agricultural subsidies and divert the majority of the aid to producers rather than traders.
"This is a general trend all over the world," Tarjan said.
The compromise is subject to the approval of the Hungarian government and the WTO, Balas said. The government is to discuss the deal on July 24.
